page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by a dedicated AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processor. It features 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at 3.3 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, alongside a bundled 950 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results show strong performance in single-threaded tasks, with Geekbench single-core scores and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression reaching top-tier status. Passmark memory scores also rank in the top tier, while multi-threaded decompression and Geekbench multi-core performance are rated as strong. Database operations, measured via Passmark, and static web serving throughput are also strong, though Redis SET operations and LLM inference for 7B models fall into average categories.

The arm64 architecture offers high resource density and power efficiency, which translates to qualitative cost advantages for workloads that can run natively on ARM. The inclusion of a 950 GB local NVMe SSD provides high-speed local storage without the added cost of external block storage. However, tradeoffs include the lack of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX, and a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps, which may limit highly distributed network-bound applications.

This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, local database hosting, web serving, software compilation, and text processing tasks that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high-speed local NVMe storage.
